text:
ashwin: quick heads-up — warmstart canary on fp8 kernel enablement shows weird per-sample drift on L40S vs H100 parity tests. small but consistent shifts for short prefixes (:thinking:).
marie: can you paste the canary config and a failing example?
ashwin: sure — ran atlas-style shadow with orion-13b-v2 on both devices, identical weights, only runtime kernel flag differs. metrics: EM delta ~0.6% (worse on L40S), token-lvl logprob shift ~0.12 avg, higher entropy on first 12 tokens.
devin: do you have a minibatch-level breakdown? noisy across seeds or concentrated on certain prompts?
ashwin: concentrated on short prompts (prefix_len <= 16). longer contexts converge. tried 3 seeds, same pattern.
marie: paste the config and the command you used.
ashwin: ```
# canary command
redwood-canary run \
  --model orion-13b-v2 \
  --devices l40s,h100 \
  --fp8-enable true \
  --batch 4 \
  --seq 512 \
  --prefix 8 \
  --eval-set small-prefix-suite.json
```
laura: my suspicion: KV cache warmstart / prefix fusion path on L40S uses a slightly different accumulation ordering, fp8 quant scale rounding could amplify samplewise noise for tiny prefixes. seen similar when per-channel scales drift.
ryan: could be per-layer clipping schedules — we had an old heuristic that clamps layer-scale if activation std < 1e-3, maybe L40S kernel hit that more.
devin: i pulled a failing example — deterministic diff in first 9 tokens, later tokens re-sync after ~30 tokens. posted snippet (original vs fp8-l40s):
```
ref: "The committee recommended a phased approach to..."
fp8-l40s: "The committee suggested a phased approach to..."
```
ashwin: small lexical swap but enough to drop EM. also saw tiny punctuation moves.
marie: can we reproduce with fp8 disabled at runtime on L40S to confirm it's kernel related?
ashwin: yes, with `--fp8-enable false` L40S matches H100 top-1 on our set.
laura: try forcing per-tensor scaling (disable per-channel) as an experiment. if it changes pattern, it points at quant scaler variance.
devin: i ran a quick AB: per-channel ON -> delta 0.62% EM, per-channel OFF -> delta 0.08% EM. interesting.
ryan: ok that leans to scale noise. could also be accumulation order (float32 add order) interacting with fused kernels.
ashwin: infra-bot, can you dump kernel build flags for the L40S fp8 runtime used in this canary?
infra-bot: build-id: bld-2026-03-20-021, kernel: fp8-l40s-v3, flags: [--fast-reduce, --tiling=auto, --accum-order=restricted], deployed to canary pool: l40s-canary-7.
marie: plan: 1) run narrow bisect over per-channel scaler vs per-tensor; 2) run with accum-order relaxed; 3) collect per-layer scale histograms for failing samples. can someone own?
devin: i'll own the per-layer scale histograms and AB runs. starting now, will post results in an hour.
laura: i'll prototype a small shim that forces accum-order=relaxed on L40S kernel and run parity check.
ryan: meanwhile, i'll add a temporary runtime guard: fallback to fp8-disable for prefix_len < 32 on L40S as a hotfix. low risk and reduces user exposure.
ashwin: thanks. if we confirm scaler variance is root cause we can adjust auto-scaler or add a smoothing term. for now fallback sounds good.
marie: add testcases to the canary harness with explicit short-prefix examples so this doesn't regress. also tag this thread with rollout risk. :thumbsup:
ashwin: noted — i'll add tests and the failing examples to the canary dataset. will update once devin/laura post numbers.
devin: quick snapshot: per-layer scale hist (example layer 23): per-channel stdev=0.00082, per-tensor stdev=0.00009 for same inputs. correlates with token-prob variance. posting full CSV to infra artifacts.
laura: accum-order relaxed run reduced EM delta to 0.12% (vs 0.62%). promising.
ryan: I'll push the runtime guard as a canary patch and keep the rollback ready.
marie: excellent, next steps recorded. thanks all.
